source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Identify the primary acid-base disturbance (respiratory or metabolic) and whether compensation is occurring, guiding appropriate clinical response","B":"Diagnosing one specific underlying infection, rather than characterizing the client's broader acid-base status as intended","C":"Carrying fairly little established clinical utility despite being a routine part of interpreting a client's ABG results in practice","D":"Taking the place of any other clinical assessment the nurse would otherwise still need to perform for the client during care"}}
source_row.rationale: Systematic ABG interpretation, evaluating pH, PaCO2, and HCO3, helps identify the primary acid-base disturbance (respiratory or metabolic, acidosis or alkalosis) and whether compensation is occurring, an essential skill guiding appropriate clinical response to the underlying condition.
source_row.source_name: Clinical Respiratory References — Systematic ABG Interpretation
source_row.stem: A nurse interprets a client's arterial blood gas (ABG) results, systematically evaluating pH, PaCO2, and HCO3 to determine the acid-base status. This systematic approach helps:
